provenance.paper_title: MangaFlow: An End-to-End Agentic Framework for Controllable Story to Manga Generation

representation_paths.memory_component: story-section memory: cached visual reference images for shared scenes, characters and key objects (R_k^scene, R_k^char, R_k^obj)

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.4 Story Section Memory; Sec. 3.6 reference-conditioned rendering
evidence.figure_or_table: Equation 6 (M_k = (d_k, R_k^scene, R_k^char, R_k^obj, phi_k)); Algorithm 1 lines 4-10
evidence.paraphrase: Each story section s_k owns a memory record keyed by section identity. The record holds generated or user-supplied reference IMAGES for the section's shared scenes, characters and key objects. Algorithm 1 loads the cached memory M_k if available and otherwise generates and stores the references; every panel assigned to section k then reads the same stored images and conditions rendering on them to preserve scene/character/object consistency. Access is by section (and entity) key, not by embedding similarity. The stored images are the artifacts themselves, so the perceptual source is directly available downstream.

representation_paths.memory_component: story-section memory: textual section description d_k and structured character / key-object profiles phi_k

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.4 Story Section Memory
evidence.paraphrase: Alongside the reference images the same record persists a textual section description d_k and structured profiles phi_k describing characters and key objects. These text records are written once per section and are re-read as prompt conditioning for every panel in that section, so they are an explicit cross-represented text memory distinct from the stored images.

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.4 Story Section Memory
evidence.paraphrase: Memory is populated lazily inside the generation loop rather than fully built up front: for each section the framework first tries to load the cached M_k, and only if it is unavailable does it generate the references and write the new record. The store therefore grows during generation under a fixed deterministic write rule, and later panels read entries written by earlier iterations. No revision, merge, or eviction of existing entries is described.

derived.hybrid_relation: The cached reference images and the textual section description / structured profiles live in one section record and are jointly supplied to the panel renderer, which conditions on the images while being prompted with the text profiles.

adjudication_notes: Full text read via arXiv HTML; inclusion is clear (persistent cross-panel visual reference memory is a core contribution, and images are what is stored and reused).

Tier T2: Algorithm 1 shows generate-if-absent-then-cache executing inside the panel-generation loop, so persistent memory content is created during the deployed generation run and consumed by later panels under a fixed rule. This matches the corpus treatment of generation-pipeline systems that write to a reference store during downstream generation (gest.json and canvas.json), and differs from formation-stage expansion completed before downstream traversal (videotree.json). T3 is ruled out because no deployment-time feedback changes a write, maintenance, or retrieval policy.
No inference-time revision, summarization, deduplication, or eviction of memory entries is described.
